The Leqtique - 11/11 uses a special IC, the NJM2073D, which was discontinued shortly after its release. As a result, only a small amount was manufactured at the time of its release in 2018, with no prospect of it ever being reproduced. However, a few years ago, a second-source version of the same IC was released, and we have now successfully converted it into an EVR with some updates. The range of each control is the same as the original Leqtique - 11/11, except for the gain control, which has a slightly expanded maximum value. While retaining the original Leqtique's greatest features, such as its extreme response to guitar volume and the unique frequency, Q settings, and feel of each tone shape control from the 11/11, the basic design has been completely revamped to include EVR. As an additional update, there are two small switches built inside. Because the 11/11 is an effect that is constructed purely with a multi-stage configuration, in which the vacuum tubes of an actual amplifier are replaced with Power ICs (as with the 9/9, 10/10, etc., it does not include signal clipping caused by diodes), by adjusting the low end of the distortion section of each stage, it is possible to make comprehensive adjustments to the texture of the distortion, the tightness/looseness of the sound, the texture of the compression, etc. The 11/11 pushes the distortion possibilities of the "Distortion" to their limits, and at high gain it also has a "Fuzz"-like quality. This characteristic can be further strengthened or weakened to create a tighter, more dynamic sound. The Leqtique brand is fundamentally a brand that continues to explore the possibilities of distortion across the entire gain range, from low gain to high gain, and I believe that some of the sound characteristics of the 11/11 have been perfected to the point that it's hard to imagine any ideas or concepts that could surpass them even in 2025. Please take a look at the demo video by official demonstrator Jake Cloudchair, which compares the 9/9 - 10/10 - 11/11, as it's very easy to understand. Shun Nokina About the "EVR" concept Since 2019, I have been based in Europe and have been involved in the design of several pedals, but the Leqtique pedal line has essentially been on hiatus without releasing any new products. However, by temporarily moving my base to Iceland in 2024, I was able to gain some wonderful inspiration, and have continued to design all of them as an updated package called "EVR." "EVR" is the Icelandic word for Europe. The letters strongly evoke the idea that the pedals embody the inspiration and experiences gained over many years of traveling and living in various parts of Europe. The Leqtique pedals originally embodied a strong desire for Europe, with their vibrant paintwork and dark sound, but now they are more clearly embodied as a more real-world experience. Leqtique pedals, which have not received an update in 15 years, have been completely redesigned from the ground up, including the housing, all components, and concept. For example, the housing, which was previously a one-piece machined aluminum body, has been redesigned from a standard "box" design with a wide tolerance range, but has been completely redesigned specifically for the Leqtique EVR pedal. By rethinking the advantages of a one-piece design, the previously aluminum-only construction has been divided and integrated into three sections: a functional aluminum base case, a non-magnetic stainless steel cosmetic layer, and individually machined parts.
